verdict: Approve. Both prior blockers resolved: catch now wraps only service.list with a single own-signal abort check on each continuation, and the open-failure path (failure after onStart) has a regression test that also caught a real getUI bug. Revised lesson is sound within stated scope. Based on supplied diff only; nothing run by reviewer.
risks: If applying results throws, status stays 'loading' with records already cleared and no recovery path. This is intended and asserted, but readers may copy it without noticing the stuck state.

listenTo(status, 'retry', this.loadRecords) drops the returned promise, so a defect during Retry becomes an unhandled rejection. Acceptable as bug surfacing; one doc clause would stop agents adding a reflexive .catch.
In openRecords, a throwing stop() inside the catch replaces the original error and skips showError. Minor, because the original error is logged first.
Close while start() is still pending relies on the framework's preparation/stop ordering and is untested. Acceptable because lifecycle edge cases are deferred to reference docs.
missingTests: Optional: an end-to-end Close clicked while the child start() is still pending, if that ordering is meant to be supported.
Optional: Retry clicked twice quickly, showing through the UI that the newer load aborts the earlier one (the controlled-service probes already cover the logic).
simplifications: The `this.run === run` check in the before:destroy listener can likely go, since releaseRun already stops listening to the old run's view; keeping it is cheap.
loadRecords' true/false return value is only used by tests and could be dropped; harmless if kept as documentation.
nextSteps: Rerun the two deliberate-defect checks (remove the success guard, remove the error guard) against the simplified single-check code before committing.
Finish the local link check for README, config, CSS and JSON.
Commit and open a same-repo PR against master on the marionettejs org remote.
